column1: # Gap 278's bounded remedy: the (function, jurisdiction) -> verdict table AS DATA.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.  P764: `algorithm0r/canvas-lms-mcp` is MIT and exposes grading,
# comments and rubrics.  It clears every licence check this KB has ever written and is
# GATED-to-PROHIBITED in several jurisdictions.  A licence-only shelf keeps admitting
# architectures that cannot be deployed.  Passes 59 and 60 wrote the two-axis pre-flight as
# PROSE in `compose/patterns.md`; prose is not readable by an instrument, so this is the data.
# BAND -- READ THIS BEFORE CITING ANY ROW.  Every row is `reported`, and that is not
# modesty, it is a measured property of the channel (Gap 270, re-posed pass 61):
#   - 12 of 12 primary policy hosts answer 000 to curl, AND so do example.com, google.com
#     and wikipedia, while raw.githubusercontent.com / pypi / npm answer 200.  The proxy
#     names the mechanism itself: `connect_rejected`, "gateway answered 403 to CONNECT".
#   - WebFetch against the same hosts returns EGRESS_BLOCKED.
#   So this session has exactly ONE regulatory channel -- a search backend's server-side
#   fetch -- and ZERO direct-fetch channels.  No row here can be payload-read, and no row
#   can be cross-checked against a second INDEPENDENT oracle.  A `verified` band on a
#   policy row in this KB would therefore be a defect, today and in any session that
#   measures the same egress policy.
# VERDICT vocabulary.  DECLARED CLOSED AT FIVE VALUES, AND THE DATA HAS CARRIED MORE THAN FIVE
# SINCE PASS 269.  p270 reconciles the header to the data rather than leaving a filter to
# discover the drift at runtime.  This is the same defect class as T29: a statement ABOUT the
# file disagreed with the file, and the statement was the thing being trusted.
#   -- the original five --
#   PROHIBITED           - the function may not be deployed at all
#   GATED                - deployable subject to named obligations (assessment, oversight, logging)
#   MANDATED             - the jurisdiction REQUIRES the function be taught/performed
#   PROPOSED             - a bill or draft, not in force; never plan against this
#   UNREGULATED          - searched and nothing specific found.  An informed gap, not a green light.
#   -- in the data since p269, undeclared until p270 --
#   NONE_IN_FORCE        - an instrument EXISTED and is abrogated/withdrawn.  Not the same as
#                          UNREGULATED: something was repealed, so do not read it as a greenfield.
#   ADOPTED              - a policy or strategy is adopted.  NOT a binding obligation on a
#                          deliverable; pairs with a separate function row for what actually binds.
#   IN_FORCE_UNENFORCED  - law is in force and enforcement is absent or suspended.  Scope the
#                          engagement on ADOPTION risk, not penalty risk (KR by grace period,
#                          JP by statutory design -- same value, different mechanism, see notes).
#   -- also in the data, undeclared, found by COUNTING the column instead of reading the header --
#   HIGH_RISK            - the instrument classifies the function as high-risk WITHOUT yet
#                          naming the obligations.  Weaker than GATED, which names them.
#                          Sole occupant: VN assessment_grading under Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg --
#                          and see that row's UNRECONCILED note, p269: VN carries TWO instruments
#                          for this one (function, jurisdiction) and no shelf has reconciled them.
#   FRAMEWORK_LAUNCHED   - a competency//capability framework is published by or with the
#                          ministry.  Implies a TEACHER-FACING deliverable, not a compliance one.
#                          Sole occupant: EG teacher_competency (UNESCO + MoETE, 2026-06-03).
#   -- added by p270, because five of its rows had no honest home in the ten above --
#   ADVISORY_NONBINDING  - a NAMED, DATED, non-binding instrument exists: voluntary framework,
#                          "strongly recommends", encouraged principles, national priority.
#                          THE MOST COMMON STATE IN THIS FIELD and the one the original five
#                          could not express: UNREGULATED would claim nothing was found, which
#                          is false and reads as a green light; MANDATED would invent a duty.
#   NOT_ESTABLISHED      - this base LOOKED and could not establish the row.  Distinct from
#                          UNREGULATED, which asserts the jurisdiction has no rule; this asserts
#                          only that WE do not know, and names the query that would settle it.
# 🔴 ANY FILTER OR COMPILER READING THIS FILE MUST HANDLE TWELVE VALUES, NOT FIVE.  The count
# was reached by `cut -f4 | sort -u` on the data, NOT by reading this header -- which is the only
# method that found HIGH_RISK and FRAMEWORK_LAUNCHED at all.  A consumer
# that switches on the original five will silently drop every ZA, KR, JP, NC, EE, FI, NL, SG,
# ID, CO, CL, BR and regional row -- i.e. most of the non-US-state coverage this base has.
# REGION vocabulary (closed, five values, per the KB-wide convention):
#   North America | EMEA | APAC | LATAM | Global
# Columns: region

column1: North America
column6: NC AI Leadership Council AI Strategic Roadmap
column7: NEW p270. DPI "strongly recommends" districts review incumbent EdTech providers deploying GenAI and vet them for safety, privacy, reliability and efficacy. NO method specified, so district practice will vary. Same commencement date as s.7.39 above and NOT the same instrument - NC runs THREE layers (2024-01-16 DPI guidebook, this Roadmap, the statute). They LAYER, they do not contradict (contrast VN, which does). ADOPTION COUNTER-EVIDENCE: WRAL Feb 2026 - only ~1/3 of NC district leaders had given students any GenAI training.

column1: North America
column6: DOL Training and Employment Notice No. 07-25
column7: NEW p270, and the instrument now has a citable identifier it lacked in the register. FIVE content areas (AI principles / potential uses / directing AI / evaluating outputs / responsible use) + SEVEN delivery principles (incl. experiential learning, embedding learning in context, complementary human skills). Explicitly VOLUNTARY - imposes no new regulatory requirement. Named audiences: workforce boards, community colleges, Job Corps centres. Sits atop DOL guidance permitting WIOA funds and governor's reserve monies for AI skilling, so it is a FUNDING instrument, not a compliance one. Identifier rendering UNRECONCILED: one source gives TEGL 07-25.

column1: EMEA
column7: NEW p270. Among the FIRST countries in Europe to put AI literacy formally into the national curriculum (Tallinn University study of a 2024 national survey, n=15,631, grades 6-12). Deployment is a MEASURED FACT, not a plan: Education and Research Minister Kristina Kallas told Politico in May 2026 that ~half of the country's 20,000 upper-secondary students were on an OpenAI-partnered platform, rest expected that summer. NOTE for a sovereignty conversation: what is deployed at national scale is a PROPRIETARY US platform. Commencement date NOT established - do not quote one.

column1: EMEA
column6: Ministry of Education and Culture national priority
column7: NEW p270. Finland has built NO standalone AI subject; AI literacy is integrated into existing subjects via "phenomenon-based learning". MoEC names AI skills a national priority across all education levels, with teacher support and safe use as focus areas. Entered ADVISORY_NONBINDING deliberately: a national priority plus curricular integration was located, a binding instrument was NOT. A Finnish engagement is a cross-curricular integration problem, not a course-delivery one.

column1: EMEA

Costed next step, NOT run this pass: Dutch-language queries against the Ministerie van OCW and SLO.

column1: APAC
column7: NEW p270. Voluntary adoption of transparency, fairness, ethics, human oversight and accountability; the AI Verify toolkit is OPTIONAL. Consequence for an education deliverable: the binding constraints are procurement, data residency and curriculum alignment - NOT an AI statute. Context: 56% of SG enterprises report progress toward scaled AI adoption, the regional high.

column1: APAC

column1: APAC
column7: NEW p270 - public-appetite datum, not an instrument, entered because clients ask for it by name. Support for BANNING AI in schools: Indonesia 23%, Singapore 28%, Japan 29%, Malaysia 29%, South Korea 31%. EVERY figure below one third. The "parents will not accept it" objection is unsupported in APAC by this measure. KR's position as regional high is consistent with T22's documented rollout failure rather than with general hostility.

column1: LATAM
column7: NEW p270. The ILIA regional index rates Brazil the region's GOVERNANCE LEADER on the strength of a robust national strategy - which sits alongside PL 2.338/2023 still being PENDING in the Camara dos Deputados after Senate approval in Dec 2024 (row above). Strategy adopted, statute not passed: both true, and a client slide must not merge them.

column1: LATAM
column7: NEW p270. A Universidad Autonoma de Madrid analysis finds NO unified regulatory framework for AI in Latin American HIGHER education, with most universities operating without clear internal rules and deciding in isolation. This is the INSTITUTION-level inverse of the school-level pattern this base documents for LATAM, and it is directly monetisable: the first deliverable for a LATAM university client is frequently the policy and governance scaffold, not the tutor.
